subject: Nanotechnology
title: Nano Coatings for Energy
description: Learn Nano Coatings for Energy in one minute.

hook.text: Solar panels lose 4 percent efficiency to surface reflection — nano anti-reflective coatings recover most of that lost light.

buildup.text: Moth-eye nanostructures create a gradient refractive index — light enters without the abrupt reflection of a flat surface.

discovery.text: Self-cleaning superhydrophobic coatings on solar panels prevent dust accumulation — maintaining peak efficiency without washing.

twist.text: Anti-reflective and self-cleaning coatings have conflicting requirements — one needs texture, the other needs smoothness.

climax.text: Hierarchical moth-eye structures with hydrophobic tips achieve both — anti-reflective and self-cleaning in one nano surface.

punchline.text: A moth's eye and a lotus leaf combined — one nano surface does both.

quiz.question: How do moth-eye nanostructures reduce surface reflection?
options: They absorb reflected light and convert it to heat
They create a gradient refractive index that eliminates the abrupt interface where reflection occurs
They scatter light in all directions to prevent specular reflection
